dallas-baps-mandir-diwali-annakut-firewo.headline: Dallas BAPS Mandir Expects 12,000 for Diwali Annakut and Fireworks on November 10
dallas-baps-mandir-diwali-annakut-firewo.body:
• The BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Irving expects roughly 12,000 visitors for its Diwali and Hindu New Year celebration on Tuesday, November 10, from 3:00 p.m. to 8:00 p.m.
  • The centrepiece is the Annakut, an offering of hundreds of vegetarian dishes prepared by devotees, alongside an exhibition titled "Light Beyond Lamps: Journey Through Hindu Sanskruti" and a closing fireworks and light-and-sound show.
  • BAPS Charities will make a food donation to Irving Cares as part of the event; its Dallas-area drive for the same nonprofit collected about 2,000 pounds of food in October 2025.
  • No ticket or registration details have been published for the BAPS event — Dallas-area readers should confirm entry arrangements on the mandir's page before travelling; the Radha Krishna Temple of Dallas in Allen runs its own Diwali programme November 5-10.

Dallas-Fort Worth's Diwali season peaks on Tuesday, November 10, when the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Irving hosts its Diwali and Hindu New Year celebration and expects roughly 12,000 visitors over the course of the day. The event runs from 3:00 p.m. to 8:00 p.m., two days after Diwali itself, which falls on Sunday, November 8 this year, Hoodline reported.

Annakut at the Centre

The afternoon is built around the Annakut, the traditional mountain of food offered to the deities for the Hindu New Year. BAPS describes the offering as hundreds of vegetarian dishes — snacks, sweets and savouries prepared by devotees and presented in gratitude — set against handcrafted Diwali decor. Visitors can also walk through an immersive exhibition, "Light Beyond Lamps: Journey Through Hindu Sanskruti," which explores Hindu values and traditions; Hoodline reported the same theme is being used across BAPS mandirs throughout North America for this year's Diwali and New Year celebrations.

The programme also weaves in the United States' 250th anniversary and a tribute to frontline heroes, with a dedicated stage segment and planned flag processions, before closing with a fireworks show and a light-and-sound experience.

Service Alongside Celebration

BAPS Charities, the organisation's humanitarian arm, will make a charitable food donation benefiting Irving Cares, a local nonprofit, as part of the event. The pairing has local history: a BAPS Charities food drive in the Dallas area from October 4 to 21, 2025, also for Irving Cares, collected about 2,000 pounds of food from volunteers of varied ages and backgrounds.

The Wider Dallas Diwali Week

The BAPS celebration caps a full week of Diwali programming across the metroplex. The Radha Krishna Temple of Dallas in Allen runs its Diwali Mahotsav from November 5 to 10, including the lighting of 11,111 diyas on Saturday, November 7, from 6:00 p.m., Lakshmi Puja on November 8 — the temple lists the Drik Panchang muhurat for Dallas as 5:52 to 7:46 p.m. CST — an Annakoot on November 9, cultural performances, a food festival and fireworks. A Frisco Diwali Mela is also scheduled for November 1 at Kaleidoscope Park, with dance, a talent stage, a kids' fun zone and vendors.

Planning Your Visit

Hoodline's report lists no ticket price, registration or RSVP requirement for the November 10 BAPS event, and the mandir's own page is the place to confirm entry and parking arrangements before setting out: see the BAPS Dallas mandir page. With 12,000 visitors expected across five hours, arriving early in the 3:00 p.m. window is the practical move for families who want the Annakut darshan and the exhibition before the evening fireworks crowd builds.

times-square-diwali-countdown-2026.headline: Times Square Rings In Diwali With Diya Countdown and Concert
times-square-diwali-countdown-2026.body:
• Diwali at Times Square held its 11th edition on Saturday, October 24, 2026, closing with a Diya Lighting Ceremony and a countdown on the One Times Square Ball Drop Tower screen.
  • Kanika Kapoor, Raja Kumari, Rishi Singh and Shanmukha Priya headlined the Light Up Times Square Concert, after a day that included a Diwali Bazaar, a Kids Zone and the “Colors of India and America” dance showcase.
  • The festival is an early celebration: Diwali itself falls on Sunday, November 8, 2026, and the holiday has been a New York City public school holiday since 2023.
  • Admission was free, and Colors TV, the festival’s media partner, broadcast the celebration for viewers who could not attend in person.

Times Square marked Diwali on Saturday, October 24, with the 11th edition of Diwali at Times Square, a day-long festival that ended with dignitaries lighting a diya as a countdown ran on the Ball Drop Tower screen at One Times Square. The celebration, organized by Sammaan For All and presented by P&G and Tide and Toyota, brought a Diwali Bazaar, cultural performances and a headline concert to the blocks around Broadway, according to the organizer’s announcement carried by PR Newswire.

A Countdown Borrowed From New Year’s Eve

The evening ceremony is the festival’s signature moment. After an afternoon of performances, dignitaries joined together for the Diya Lighting Ceremony, with the countdown displayed on the same tower screen that counts down the New Year’s Eve ball drop, leading into the Light Up Times Square Concert. Secret NYC, previewing the event, described it as the largest Diwali festival outside India and noted that New York City has partnered with the festival since 2024. The city declared October 29, 2023, “Diwali at Times Square Day.”

https://x.com/PTI_News/status/2114245609507160273

The wider program began a day earlier. An awards and gala dinner on October 23 at Tribeca 360 honored Indian Americans for contributions to philanthropy, innovation, medicine and entrepreneurship, according to IndiaWest. On October 24, the Kids Zone offered diya painting, rangoli activities and Bollywood dance lessons, alongside product sampling and educational displays from festival partners.

Concert Lineup and a Day of Programming

The afternoon showcase, “Colors of India and America,” featured Indian, Indo-Caribbean and Hispanic dance groups. The closing concert lineup mixed Bollywood and Indian-American acts: Filmfare Award-winning singer Kanika Kapoor, Grammy-nominated rapper Raja Kumari, Indian Idol 13 winner Rishi Singh and Indian Idol 12 finalist Shanmukha Priya, along with singer-rapper Sparsh Shah, known as “Purhythm,” New York’s Kunal Lamba and New Jersey singer Saanvi Nacha.

The Consulate General of India in New York hosted a press conference for the festival on October 14, where Deputy Consul General Vishal Harsh expressed support for the celebration. In a message, Consul General Binaya S. Pradhan framed the festival as part of the relationship between the two countries.

"Diwali celebrates the triumph of light over darkness, knowledge over ignorance, and hope over despair. I commend Sammaan For All-Diwali At Times Square for bringing communities together in one of the world's most iconic public spaces to share the joy of this festival."

— Binaya S. Pradhan, Consul General of India in New York

Neeta Bhasin, the founder and creator of Diwali at Times Square, said the event aims to instill pride in South Asian American youth in their heritage and to promote the values of art, culture and togetherness associated with Diwali, according to IndiaWest. Sponsors included Gopi as platinum sponsor, Xoom by PayPal as gold sponsor and the State Bank of India.

Why the Festival Lands Before Diwali Itself

The October 24 date is deliberate. Diwali in 2026 falls on Sunday, November 8, so the Times Square celebration functions as a public kickoff two weeks ahead of the holiday, on a weekend when a street festival can draw a full-day crowd. The pattern is consistent across the United States, where the largest public Diwali events are typically scheduled on the weekends before the day itself, while November 8 is kept for home and temple observances. Diwali has been a New York City public school holiday since 2023, though in 2026 it falls on a Sunday.

What Comes Next

For diaspora families in the New York area, the Times Square festival is the season’s opener rather than its finale. Community and temple celebrations continue through the November 8 holiday, and Colors TV’s broadcast of the Times Square program extends the event to viewers outside the city. The festival’s second decade now rests on a fixed formula — bazaar, cultural showcase, diya countdown, concert — that has made Diwali part of Times Square’s annual calendar alongside its better-known New Year’s Eve countdown.

indian-woman-fined-2500-molesting-singap.headline: Indian Woman Fined S$2,500 for Molesting Singapore Nightclub Server
indian-woman-fined-2500-molesting-singap.body:
• Sonik Archana Susheel, 32, an Indian national, pleaded guilty to one count of molestation and was fined S$2,500 on October 29 in Singapore.
  • The victim, 20, a nightclub server whose identity is protected by a gag order, said she was fired after the March incident and lost about S$18,000, roughly six months of income.
  • Sonik had voluntarily paid the victim S$1,500; the court made no further compensation order, saying there was not enough evidence to decide the claim and that it should be pursued elsewhere.
  • Under Singapore law, molestation can bring up to two years in jail, a fine, caning, or a combination; women are exempted from caning.

A Singapore court fined an Indian national S$2,500 (US$1,950) on Thursday, October 29, after she pleaded guilty to molesting a female server at a downtown nightclub. The victim told the court she was fired after the incident and asked for additional compensation, which the court declined to order.

What Happened at the Nightclub

Sonik Archana Susheel, 32, went to the nightspot at around 11pm on March 13 to meet a friend, according to court reporting by CNA. She had consumed alcohol at home and continued drinking at the club. CNA is not naming the club, as doing so could lead to the victim's identification.

https://x.com/malaymail/status/2115712590827372553

After midnight on March 14, Sonik was dancing alone when the victim and two colleagues walked through the area. The victim, a "bottle girl" — a waitress who specialises in delivering entire bottles of liquor to tables — nearly collided with Sonik, who was dancing erratically. According to The Straits Times, Sonik touched the victim's buttocks and pushed her stomach area. Court documents stated the entire interaction lasted not more than five seconds. The Straits Times account also reported that she showed the victim the middle finger.

The victim sought help from the nightspot's bouncers. Her superiors told her to rest, later reported the incident to the police, and Sonik was arrested that same day.

The Court Hearing

Deputy Public Prosecutor Yohanes Ng sought a fine of S$2,500. Defence lawyer Ariffin Sha, from Shehzhadee Law in the CNA account, said the prosecution's position was fair. He said his client had no prior convictions and had voluntarily paid compensation of S$1,500 to the victim. In the Straits Times account, the court heard the offence was not premeditated. The defence also said her actions were entirely out of character and were not for the purposes of sexual gratification.

"As a result of this case, I was subsequently fired from the job."

— The victim, addressing the court

The Victim's Compensation Claim

The victim attended the hearing and confirmed she had received the S$1,500 voluntary payment, but she asked for additional compensation. She said she was removed from her work group chat a week after the incident and removed from all her schedules in the following month. She put her lost income at about S$18,000, about six months of pay, and said she subsequently left the industry altogether because of the mental distress she faced.

According to Goody Feed, Principal District Judge Lee Lit Cheng said there was not enough evidence to decide what compensation, if any, was owed. The judge added that the claim should be pursued elsewhere and made no order, since S$1,500 had already been paid. The defence had argued that the earlier payment covered emotional harm and that the link between the offence and the job loss was unclear.

What the Law Provides, and What Remains Open

For molestation, an offender in Singapore can be jailed for up to two years, fined, caned, or given any combination of those punishments, and women are exempted from caning. In this case the sentence was a fine, following a guilty plea, no prior convictions, and the voluntary compensation already paid.

For Indian nationals working and socialising in Singapore, the case is a straight factual record of how a brief incident in a nightclub moved through the courts: arrest on the day, a guilty plea, a S$2,500 fine, S$1,500 paid to the victim, and a compensation dispute the criminal court left to be pursued elsewhere. Whether the victim pursues that claim through another route has not been reported.

ajit-kaur-missing-ceres-woman-found-cana.headline: Missing Ceres Woman Ajit Kaur, 72, Found Dead in Canal After Two-Month Search
ajit-kaur-missing-ceres-woman-found-cana.body:
• Ajit Kaur, 72, was found dead on October 24 in the Lower Lateral 3 Canal near Central Avenue and Keyes Road in Ceres, California, and formally identified on October 27.
  • She had been missing since August 23, when she was last seen at about 1:45 a.m. near Whitmore Avenue and Mitchell Road, close to her apartment complex.
  • The two-month search involved canal patrols, a tracking K-9 from Merced County and a Stanislaus County dive unit using an underwater sonar drone.
  • Police say the investigation into her death is ongoing. Anyone with information can contact Detective Sergeant Berber at 209-538-5672.

A two-month search for a missing California woman has ended with the discovery of her body in an irrigation canal. The Stanislaus County Coroner's Office identified the woman as Ajit Kaur, 72, according to a Ceres Police Department statement reported by People. Kaur, an Indian-origin resident of Ceres, had been missing since late August.

Found during a routine canal patrol

An employee of the Turlock Irrigation District (TID) found Kaur's remains on Saturday, October 24, in the Lower Lateral 3 Canal near Central Avenue and Keyes Road in Ceres, during one of the district's multiple daily patrols of the canal system. Officers confirmed the remains were human, and the coroner's office made the formal identification on Tuesday, October 27.

https://x.com/modbee/status/2116017356619080010

Missing since August 23

Kaur was reported missing from the Casa Grande Apartment complex in the 3100 block of Whitmore Avenue on August 23. She was last seen that day at approximately 1:45 a.m. near Whitmore Avenue and Mitchell Road. Detectives said their investigation led them to believe she may have entered the TID canal located east of the apartment complex, which runs parallel to Moore Road near Whitmore Avenue.

An extensive search

Police said they pursued available leads and canvassed the surrounding area, including canal banks throughout Ceres. The Merced County Sheriff's Office provided a K-9 trained to track missing people, and the Stanislaus County Sheriff's Department Dive Unit scanned the canals with an underwater remote sonar drone. Detectives also worked with TID to map the water routes Kaur could have taken and whether she could have reached the district's regulating reservoir.

"The Ceres Police Department extends its heartfelt condolences to Kaur's family and loved ones during this difficult time."

— Ceres Police Department

A canal network that complicates searches

Ceres, a city of roughly 50,000 in Stanislaus County in California's Central Valley, is crossed by the Turlock Irrigation District's canal network, which carries water to farms across the region. The canals are patrolled several times a day by district staff — the patrol rhythm that eventually located Kaur — but the moving water and the network's regulating reservoirs make searches slow: investigators had to model which channels a person entering near Whitmore Avenue could have been carried through before narrowing the area to search with sonar.

Investigation continues

Police have not announced a cause of death, and the investigation remains open. Kaur's disappearance and the two months that followed were a sustained concern for the area's South Asian community, for whom elderly relatives living alone — and walking alone at night — are a familiar family worry. Anyone with additional information is asked to contact Detective Sergeant Berber of the Ceres Police Department at 209-538-5672.
